experiment: Vol.1-B · closed-loop concurrency with NVIDIA AIPerf · profile R · RAG-shaped
written_before: the NIM container launch for this profile; p17_run_profile.sh refuses to start if this file or its .sha256 is missing or changed, or if the run directory exists
runs: one main run; plus one fresh-container run each at concurrency 128 and 256 after the main run; not repeated to obtain a different outcome

stack.env: NIM_MAX_MODEL_LEN=8192 · VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 · all other NIM settings default · no Guardrails
stack.max_num_seqs: 256 — not set by NIM (no override found in the image's NIM packages, manifests or environment), so vLLM's default applies: vllm/engine/arg_utils.py get_batch_defaults gives 256 for GPUs with < 70 GiB (OpenAI API server). Read inside the running container on 2026-09-15. Checked against the server's num_requests_running during the run.
stack.kv_cache: 81,360 tokens, block size 16, prefix caching enabled, gpu_memory_utilization clamped by NIM to 0.8588 (desktop memory in use) — from the server's /metrics at READY in the calibration container; recorded again at READY for this run
stack.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 32 GB, driver 591.86 / CUDA 13.1

tool.name: NVIDIA AIPerf
tool.token_counts: server-reported usage (--use-server-token-count); tokenizer files copied from the NIM model cache
tool.definitions: AIPerf's own: ITL excludes the first token; total output token throughput over the benchmark duration; not changed

instrument_check.basis: judged on the agreement of ITL, e2e and the TTFT floor (min, and p50 in the 127.0.0.1 run). TTFT avg/p50 exceeded 20% in some client runs; this verdict is a human judgement written after seeing the data, not a pre-set statistic.

load.mode: closed loop, --concurrency N (a new request is issued as soon as one completes)
load.per_level: --warmup-request-count N at concurrency N (excluded) · --benchmark-duration D · --benchmark-grace-period 0 (requests unfinished at D are not counted, so the drain tail is excluded) · D = min(600, max(60, 4 × previous level's p99 request latency × N / N_prev)) · completed < 3N flagged, not repeated
load.container: one container for all levels of the main run; READY, then the first request is sent and discarded; server settings read at READY

deviations_listed_not_absorbed: synthetic prompt text from AIPerf's generator; prefix caching (server default) stays on
Docker Desktop port forwarding on Windows between client and server (same as all Vol.1 measurements)
server metrics window includes each level's warm-up requests
grace period 0: requests that are still running when the duration ends are dropped, which can under-count the slowest requests of a level
this measurement has no accuracy gate (synthetic input); it must not be placed next to MLPerf submissions

analysis_rules.preconditions_per_level: AIPerf exit 0 with summary · 0 request errors · instrument check passed. If any fails, that level's SLO verdicts are null.

slo.server: TTFT p99 <= 2000 ms and ITL p99 <= 100 ms
slo.interactive: TTFT p99 <= 500 ms and ITL p99 <= 30 ms

analysis_rules.N_x: largest measured concurrency such that it and every lower measured level pass SLO x; 0 if concurrency 1 fails; the largest passing level is also reported when not contiguous
analysis_rules.throughput_saturation: first level whose total output token throughput rises < 10% over the previous level
analysis_rules.memory_ceiling: first level with preemptions > 0, or requests waiting while running max is below both the level and max_num_seqs
analysis_rules.batch_cap: first level whose running max reaches max_num_seqs
analysis_rules.program: vol1b/scripts/p17_analyze.py (self-test 9 cases; 7 mutations each make a case fail)

predictions.1_record: record N_server, N_interactive (with total output tokens/s at N), the throughput saturation point, the memory ceiling level, the batch cap level and max_num_seqs for this profile. No direction is predicted.

2_memory_ceiling.claim: the memory ceiling appears at about 28 ± 8 concurrent requests — a paper estimate, not a measurement
2_memory_ceiling.paper_account: KV per token = 2 × 32 layers × 8 KV heads × 128 dim × 2 bytes = 128 KiB; 4,000 tokens per request ⇒ 512 MiB; about 14 GiB for KV on a 32 GB card ⇒ about 28 requests
2_memory_ceiling.on_the_level_grid: the first flagged level only brackets the ceiling: flagged first at 32 means the ceiling is in 17–32; at 64 means 33–64; at 16 means ≤ 16. Reading: first at 32 ⇒ consistent with 20–36 (the grid cannot exclude 17–19); first at 16 ⇒ below the claim; first at 64 ⇒ not resolved by the grid (33–36 inside, 37–64 outside); first at 128 or later, or never ⇒ above the claim. Queue-limited levels (running max reaching the level) are not memory ceilings by the analysis rule.
2_memory_ceiling.measured_input_not_used_for_the_claim: the server reported 81,360 KV tokens at READY in the calibration container; at about 4,100 tokens per request that is about 20 requests. Written here before the run; the claim above is left as given.

4_negative_control.claim: N_server of profile R < N_server of profile C
4_negative_control.if_not: ISL did not take effect — check ignore_eos and token counts before any conclusion
4_negative_control.written_after: profile C had finished (N_server 256) when this file was written; the control was defined by the work order before either run

outputs: main/levels.jsonl (one line per level, written as each level ends)
main/container/ (ctx, startup log, /metrics at READY, first request discarded)
reporting_fresh_runs: concurrency 128 and 256 are each run once more in a new container after the main run; if a level differs by more than 2× between the two runs, both sets of numbers are reported side by side, neither is chosen
